title_en: God's Being First Without Beginning, and the Coming-to-Be of Creation
body_ar:
الله تعالى هو خالق الخلق من عدم، وقد كان الله ولا شيء سواه، فله الأولية المطلقة التي لم تسبق بعدم، كما أن له الأسماء الحسنى التي أصلها ومرجعها لفظ الجلالة، وله الصفات العلا المنزهة عن كل نقص وتشبيه.
معنى العقائد:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين. يقول الشيخ حفظه الله تعالى: (العقائد). والعقائد جمع عقيدة، وهي ما يعتقده الإنسان، أي يجزم به جزماً لا يقبل الشك، والمقصود به أن هذه الأمور المذكورة هنا أكثرها أمور نصية جاءت في القرآن أو في السنة، فمن عرف أنها نصية وجب عليه الإيمان بصدقها وصحتها، ومن لم يعرف ذلك ولم يسمعها فهو غير مطالب إلا بالأصول الستة التي هي أركان الإيمان، فلا يطالب الإنسان بمعرفتها تفصيلاً إلا إذا سمع الوحي الذي نزل فيها، ومن هنا فإن كثيراً من الصفات التي تسمعونها هنا إنما جاءت في أحاديث آحاد ولم يعلّمها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لكل الأمة...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* God, exalted is He, is the creator of creation out of nothing. God was, and nothing else was with Him; so to Him belongs absolute priority, which was preceded by no non-existence. Likewise to Him belong the most beautiful names, whose root and point of reference is the name "Allah", and the most exalted attributes, which are free of every deficiency and of every likeness to created things.

## The meaning of "creed"

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and God's blessing and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and his Companions all together. The Sheikh, may God preserve him, says: *(The articles of creed.)* "ʿAqāʾid" is the plural of "ʿaqīdah", which is what a person holds as a conviction — that is, what he assents to with an assent that admits no doubt.

What is meant by it is that most of these matters mentioned here are matters established by explicit text, which have come in the Qur'an or in the sunnah. Whoever knows that they are so established, it is obligatory (wājib) upon him to believe in their truthfulness and their soundness. Whoever does not know that, and has not heard them, is not held to anything beyond the six fundamentals, which are the pillars of faith. A person is not held to knowing them in detail unless he has heard the revelation that came down concerning them. From this it follows that many of the attributes you hear of here have come only in singly transmitted reports (āḥād), and the Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, did not teach them to the whole community …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis in the middle of the argument about singly transmitted reports, and neither of the two subjects of the title — God's being first without beginning, and the coming-to-be of creation — is reached at all. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-32.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the formula introducing each quoted line of the versified creed being commented on
options: read it as the author of the versified base text, distinct from the lecturer
read it as Sheikh al-Dedew quoting his own verse
flags.note: Getting this referent wrong would misattribute a creedal formulation, so it is flagged on every record in which the formula appears. These lessons are a commentary on a versified creed (nazm): the transcriber introduces each base-text line with 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him, said', and the commentary follows. 'حفظه الله' is used of the living, which at first sight fits Sheikh al-Dedew himself. Three passages inside the run settle it otherwise. Record 719 has the speaker giving thanks for 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification' and describing what 'the Sheikh' chose to leave undetailed — a commentator does not ordinarily speak of his own base text that way while expounding it. Record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq by 'one of the scholars'. Record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. The reading adopted throughout this slice is therefore that 'the Sheikh' is the living author of the versified base text and the lecturer is his commentator. The author is nowhere named, and the identification should be confirmed by the Sheikh's office before publication, because the bracketed verse and the prose around it carry different attributions.

flags.arabic: الأولية المطلقة التي لم تسبق بعدم
flags.context: the site's synopsis, on God's priority
options: absolute priority, which was preceded by no non-existence
flags.note: A glossary homonym that must not be taken across from its usual field. 'مطلق' in legal theory is 'unqualified', the opposite of 'مقيد', and that is its glossary entry; here it is a creedal predicate meaning absolute and without any relativity — God's priority is not priority in relation to something, it is priority as such. 'Unqualified priority' would be the legal-theory reading and would empty the sentence. Note that the clause 'which was preceded by no non-existence' is the synopsis's own gloss and settles the sense.

flags.arabic: فمن عرف أنها نصية وجب عليه الإيمان بصدقها وصحتها
flags.context: the transcribed portion, in the Sheikh's own voice
options: it is obligatory (wājib) upon him to believe in their truthfulness and their soundness
he must believe them to be true and sound
he is required to accept their truth and authenticity
flags.note: A genuine legal ruling, in the Sheikh's own voice and not the site's, and the fixed mapping applies: 'obligatory (wājib)'. Two details carry weight. The obligation is conditional — it falls on 'whoever knows that they are so established' — and the English keeps the condition attached to it. And 'صحتها' here is 'their soundness', a grading of the reports, not 'their validity', since the subject is transmitted texts and not acts.

flags.arabic: فهو غير مطالب إلا بالأصول الستة التي هي أركان الإيمان
flags.context: the transcribed portion, on what a person who has not heard the texts is accountable for
options: is not held to anything beyond the six fundamentals
is only answerable for the six fundamentals
is obliged only by the six fundamentals
flags.note: The substantive claim of the record, and one that will be read closely. It limits what an individual Muslim is accountable to hold to the six pillars of faith, unless he has actually encountered the specific revealed text; and it observes that many reported attributes come only through singly transmitted reports which were not taught to the whole community. That is a recognised position with a long history, and it is also a position some readers will find surprising or will contest. It is translated exactly, neither softened nor strengthened. Crucially, the text breaks off mid-argument here: the Sheikh has stated the premise about singly transmitted reports and has not yet drawn the conclusion, so the record must not be rendered as though his position on it were complete. Style guide sections 10 and 12 both apply.

'نصي' is the adjective from 'نص', the explicit text of revelation, which the glossary fixes as 'explicit text'. The whole argument that follows turns on whether a given matter is 'نصي' and on whether the hearer knows it to be, so the term must be rendered the same way at each occurrence, which it is.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.
The one record in this run whose transcribed portion carries real doctrinal content rather than only a formula and a heading — and it breaks off in the middle of that content.

The English breaks the transcribed portion into two paragraphs where the source runs on, separating the definition of the term from the argument about what a person is accountable for. No word has been added or removed.

'المنزهة عن كل نقص وتشبيه' is rendered 'free of every deficiency and of every likeness to created things'. 'تشبيه' is the technical term for likening God to creation; 'anthropomorphism' was avoided as too narrow.
